h: Bridges, museums and a famous October fair
p: Hull is a city that rewards a bit of exploring, and an inflatable session is a great way to warm up before a wander. Arrive with a little time to spare so you can sort coats and shoes before your slot, and keep an eye on younger children on the busier slides. A pre-agreed meeting point helps, especially if you've brought a group.

Once you're back in the city centre, the Streetlife Museum is a free, family-friendly look at transport through the ages, with old trams, bikes, cars and a recreated street. Next door, Wilberforce House tells the story of William Wilberforce, the Hull-born campaigner against the slave trade. Hull Minster, the city's huge parish church, is a peaceful place to look around and is right by the cafes and bars of Trinity Square.

The Humber Bridge is an impressive sight from the Humber Bridge Country Park on the north bank, where woodland trails lead down to the foreshore for great views of the span. You can even walk part of the way across if you're brave enough. If you're in town in October, Hull Fair takes over the Walton Street area with rides, stalls and traditional fair food, and locals plan their year around it. It gets very busy, so if you're combining it with a bounce, book your session for earlier in the day. The Fruit Market area by the marina is also worth a look for its independent cafes and galleries in converted warehouses. There's plenty of parking around the city centre, but Paragon Interchange is also handy if you're arriving by train or bus.
